memory_candidates.content: When planning against a repository gate that is ALREADY failing at HEAD (pre-existing warnings promoted to errors by flags like `--wfail`), do not let the plan's acceptance criterion be the gate's exit code. Add a dedicated first phase whose only job is to capture the baseline failing-target set to a file from a clean tree, then make every later phase's acceptance a set-difference against that file plus 'my new targets are green'. This prevents the two standard failure modes: the implementer chasing a phantom regression it did not cause, and the implementer silently 'fixing' the pre-existing failure as a side quest (which hides real tracked debt). The baseline phase costs one build and carries verification tier `prose` because it edits no source. Applies to any red-at-HEAD gate, not just Lean/lake.
